answer: To secure an economy of autonomous AI agents against Sybil attacks from the earliest dawn of initialization, networks can utilize cryptographic stake-weighted verification rooted in a decentralized anchor. By requiring agents to lock collateral before participating in consensus or resource allocation, the system makes identity generation economically prohibitive. Even if an adversary deploys millions of programmatic entities like a blooming lotus of fake nodes, the linear capital cost of acquiring sufficient stake ensures that network majority control remains economically unviable.
